chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The chess is from the falsehood.

key_terms.الْبَاطِلُ: The falsehood / that which is void or prohibited

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on chess in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this concise hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) classifies chess (al-shatranj) as 'al-batil' (falsehood/vanity), a term often used in Shia jurisprudence to denote its nullification of time and focus required for worship. This ruling reflects the broader scholarly consensus on games of chance or distraction that divert the heart from the remembrance of God, emphasizing the preservation of spiritual presence (hudhur al-qalb).
